recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not reintroduce or edit the old core ShareableCodeSystem profile page for this STU3 rendering typo; if a current CRMI or external terminology profile page shows a similar rendering defect, track that separately in the owning specification/repository.
issue_request: FHIR-16872 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 Vocabulary issue for FHIR-core-CodeSystem requesting a non-substantive correction to the CodeSystem Profiles page where the ShareableCodeSystem description rendered with misleading spacing as "that share and     for Shareable Codesystem" instead of the intended description about organizations that share and publish value sets.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 14738, represented in git as f5454c4bc4 "GF#16872 - make table clearer". That commit changed source/template-profiles.html and the PageProcessor profile-list renderer so profile lists were generated with clearer Profile/Description/Context columns and without the hard-coded "for" prefix that caused the rendered spacing/confusion.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini lists CodeSystem as an active resource and the shareable logical pattern, but the active [profiles] section has no CodeSystem shareable profile entry and source/codesystem/implementationguide-CodeSystem-core.xml has no profile definitions. FHIR-37959 later removed the Shareable/Publishable/Computable/Executable profiles from core for R6 and points implementers to CRMI while retaining the profile URIs; the May 2025 Terminology minutes confirm that migration decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source change is needed because the old rendering issue was historically fixed and the specific current core profile page that displayed the bad spacing has since been removed from core.

related_jiras.note: Applied/Persuasive R6 decision removed the shareable/publishable/computable/executable profiles from core and directs implementers to CRMI, making the old core profile page out of current build scope.
Earlier no-change proposal considered moving ShareableCodeSystem and ShareableValueSet out of core before the later FHIR-37959 decision.
UTG/THO proposal linked from FHIR-37959 attempted a TI-owned profile migration but was withdrawn, so it does not require a core edit here.
